articles.title: Monotype Launches Brand Font Panel for Adobe Creative Apps
articles.summary: Monotype Connect, a new panel for Illustrator, Photoshop, and InDesign, debuted at Adobe MAX 2026 and puts teams' approved brand fonts inside the apps. It flags fonts outside a chosen library and leaves replacement to designers.

articles.title: Pentagram draws on ancient Greek coinage for Alpha Bank identity refresh
articles.summary: Pentagram has refreshed Greek financial institution Alpha Bank's identity, drawing inspiration from an ancient silver stater of Aegina that originally influenced the bank's 1972 logo. The redesigned emblem preserves the coin's distinctive geometry and subtle asymmetry, accompanied by a custom Greek and Latin typeface called Alpha Sans, an expanded color palette, and patterns derived from the symbol. Developed around the positioning "Building progress, together," the system extends across digital products, communications, and redesigned physical branches, balancing the bank's cultural heritage with a more contemporary identity.

articles.title: New camera sensor coming to the iPhone 20 Pro's main camera, says leaker
articles.summary: Apple's rumored iPhone 20 Pro could introduce a new main camera sensor manufactured using a 17-nanometer logic process. Previous reports have suggested that Apple is exploring larger camera sensors for future iPhones, including a possible 200-megapixel telephoto sensor, although the latest leak doesn't confirm whether the main sensor will grow in size. A larger sensor could improve low-light photography and overall image quality, but the specifications and potential benefits of the new component remain unknown.

articles.title: Agent Harness: Definition
articles.summary: An agent harness is the software that runs an AI model's execution loop, controls context, tool access, and limits. Two assistants built on the same model can differ sharply in capability, so UX teams should test whole tasks, not just model output.

articles.title: Google's Yi Xiang on how to build a design career across global borders
articles.summary: Google senior UX designer Yi Xiang has built an international career spanning China, Canada, Hong Kong, and the United States, learning to adapt to different creative cultures without abandoning his own perspective. His experience highlights the importance of seeking honest feedback, understanding local communication styles, and developing confidence through experimentation and continuous learning rather than trying to fit a predetermined professional identity. Creative coding and personal projects also provide opportunities to explore new technologies, develop distinctive skills, and demonstrate capabilities beyond conventional portfolio case studies.

articles.title: How to Run a UX Postmortem: A Practical Six-Step Framework
articles.summary: Design decisions should be treated as hypotheses, so teams ought to review shipped work against what users actually did. This six-step postmortem covers documenting decisions, revisiting assumptions, examining outcomes, spotting surprises, extracting principles, and storing the learning.

articles.title: UI Components for AI Agents (Website)
articles.summary: Beautifully crafted, copy-paste blocks for everything an agent shows mid-conversation: thinking states, tool calls, streaming text, tables, and more.

articles.title: Build Launch Videos from a Prompt (Website)
articles.summary: OpenMotion turns a prompt into editable motion scenes, with a real canvas and timeline to refine and export the result.

articles.title: Visual Editor for Your Codebase (Website)
articles.summary: Airship lets you edit your running app visually with Claude Code, Codex, or OpenCode. Select an element, describe the change, and watch the source update.

articles.title: Accessibility and the EU AI Act
articles.summary: The EU AI Act is already in force, with obligations phasing in through 2028, and it overlaps with accessibility law. Providers of Annex III high-risk AI must meet applicable accessibility requirements from December 2027, and people must be told, accessibly, when they deal with AI.

articles.title: April Zhu on Taste, Judgment, and Designing with AI
articles.summary: Singapore-based product designer April Zhu, trained in architecture and creator of the Colorfigures and Tinycharts AI skills, explains how she designs with AI. She left slow-moving architecture for tech's faster feedback loops, grew Colorfigures from a hand-drawn washing machine, and won't outsource her taste and judgment.

articles.title: Why Enterprise Dashboards Fail Even When They're Well Designed
articles.summary: Enterprise dashboards can fail despite excellent visual design because adoption depends on organizational trust, shared definitions, and established workflows rather than charts alone. When different departments interpret the same metrics differently, even accurate dashboards become unreliable, while competing priorities and requests for additional features can undermine their usefulness. Establishing governed metric definitions, involving stakeholders in decisions, and addressing the social dynamics surrounding data can improve adoption more effectively than repeatedly refining visual layouts.

articles.title: Working with designers
articles.summary: Designers can transform functional but ordinary interfaces into significantly better experiences, bringing a different perspective from the technical and planning-oriented culture common among engineers and product managers.

articles.title: What Makes Icons Feel Professional
articles.summary: Consistency alone does not make icons feel professional - a clear point of view, restraint, careful finishing, and a growing library do.

articles.title: UX Trends for 2027: Seven Shifts Shaping the Future of UX Design
articles.summary: Seven shifts will shape UX design in 2027, including agentic interfaces, generative UI, and AI agents as users.
